messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: GPU-SAT-2026-03-15 — autoscaling failing, queue growth in east-us-prod GPU pool

maria: getting paged — high queue depth and 5xx throttles for model-v30-context-widen in east-us-prod. dashboards show steady prefill/KV cache warmup spikes.

deploy-bot: rollout started by @ivan at 2026-03-15T02:12Z — canary traffic 10% -> v30-context-widen

ivan: rolling out v30 to improve completions but kv-cache prefill changed behavior (longer seqs). didn't expect sustained prefill on warm start.

sara: metrics: queue_length_east_us_gpu_pool = 18k, avg_token_latency spiked 8x, tail p99 > 6s. autoscaler triggered but returned errors: "scale request rejected: pool_max_capacity"

maria: confirmed. autoscaler logs: 
```
ERROR scale_manager.go:212: insufficient capacity: requested 40 gpus, pool max 32
WARN scheduler.go:98: backoff scaling; cooldown active
```

ethan: copying relevant logs, looks like the tenant pool cap prevented scaling. we have immediate queue growth and token timeouts.

ops-sre: GPU pool east-us-prod has reserved capacity commitments for other customers — can we temporarily bump burst capacity?

maria: trying emergency burst now. invoking internal quota override.

maria: `redwoodctl pools set-burst --pool east-us-prod --allow-burst 8` returned 403 (policy: no-burst-without-sales-ok).

ethan: can we reduce model resource usage short term? options: 1) revert rollout 2) throttle long-context requests 3) reroute to other regions 4) enable KV-cache prefill throttle or smaller batch size

ivan: quick rollback to previous model is the fastest. initiating canary rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback started for v30-context-widen -> v29-stable, reducing canary to 0% at 2026-03-15T02:34Z

maria: monitoring... queue length dropped ~35% after rollback but still above baseline. looks like many prefill connections remain warm and are filling KV cache.

customer-success: seeing customers in EU and NA reporting degraded response times; about 12 enterprise tenants impacted, some reporting intermittent 429s. CS is preparing templated messaging.

ethan: temporarily enabling traffic steering to fallback-models in other regions. 

maria: applying route weight change: `redwoodctl routes set-weight --model fallback-small --region west-us 0.15`

maria: route changes applied, but because many requests are sticky to east-us (latency preference), this only removed ~6% of load.

ops-sre: what about reducing max_context on the serving side? if we force truncation to 8k tokens we might reduce prefill size dramatically.

ivan: can we do a fast config toggle? there is `model-config.overrides.max_context` per route. I'll push a temporary override.

ivan: `config-api set route:/models/model-v30/max_context=8192 --reason "emit mitigation"` -> applied to routes in east-us-prod.

maria: after max_context cap, CPU/GPU memory usage per request dropped ~25%, queue reduced to ~60% of spike. p99 latency fell but still elevated.

oncall-bot: @maria handing off incident to @ethan for escalated mitigation and customer comms. Handoff at 2026-03-15T03:10Z

ethan: taking over. summary: rollout v30 caused sustained KV prefill/wider contexts => increased per-request GPU memory leading to autoscaler hitting pool cap. rolled back canary, applied max_context cap, steered some traffic to fallback models. current impact: degraded latency for some tenants, intermittent 429s resolved for most.

ethan: next steps: 1) coordinate with capacity/sales to open temporary burst quota for east-us-prod 2) throttle KV prefill (disable aggressive prefill for v30 family) 3) create internal postmortem owner and customer communication.

ops-sre: I'll open a capacity escalation ticket with infra: INCAP-1429. request: +8 GPUs in east-us-prod for 4 hours to drain queues.

maria: reducing KV prefill aggressiveness now: `feature-flags set kv_prefill_aggressive=false --target model-family:v30` -> feature flag toggled.

ivan: verifying rollout knobs: we should add a preflight check that rejects model variants which increase average sequence length beyond a configured percent. filing CI ticket.

customer-success: sending targeted notifications to affected enterprise customers with mitigation steps and ETA. Draft message ready for review.

ethan: Can support please log all escalations to a single spreadsheet and mark customers who experienced >10s p95? CS acknowledged.

customer-success: done. 12 tenants listed, 3 are marked priority (enterprise-S, enterprise-T, partner-X). Support tickets created.

ethan: quick health check: cluster queues down to 4k from 18k, p99 latency ~2.1s (baseline 0.6s), error rate dropping. Good.

maria: we should run a targeted rollout validation before reattempting v30: perf profile, kv-prefill simulation, and ramped canary with smaller context.

ethan: Agreed. assigning postmortem to @maria + @ivan. Postmortem owner: maria. Target doc link: (placeholder)

ethan: final notes: no data exfiltration, customers experienced degraded availability and elevated latency; finance impact: potential SLA credits for priority tenants — CS to estimate.

maria: incident severity set to Sev-2. beginning timeline capture.

oncall-bot: Incident update scheduled in 30m. bridge: https://join.conference/incident-3975300000

ops-sre: keep monitoring; recommended follow-up: add pre-deploy perf gate that rejects model artifacts that increase expected memory per request by >15% without explicit capacity approval.

ethan: thanks all. handing back to maria for postmortem and cleanup. :pray:
